draft.title: Carbon-13 NMR
card: In carbon-13 NMR, carbon-13 nuclei in a molecule absorb radio waves in a strong magnetic field. The spectrum shows one peak for each different carbon environment.
Carbons are in the same environment when they are bonded in the same way and the molecule is symmetrical about them. These carbons give one shared peak.

So the number of peaks equals the number of different kinds of carbon, not the total number of carbons. Propane, CH3CH2CH3, has three carbons but two peaks, because the two end carbons are equivalent.
The position of a peak is its chemical shift. It depends on what the carbon is bonded to, so carbons next to an oxygen appear at a different shift from carbons in a plain chain.
draft.remember: One peak for each kind of carbon: count environments, not carbon atoms.

a.q: A molecule has four carbon atoms, and its carbon-13 NMR spectrum shows three peaks. What does this tell you?
opts: Two of the carbons are in the same environment
One carbon gives no signal in the spectrum
Three of the carbons are bonded to oxygen
The molecule must contain three double bonds
a.why: Each different carbon environment gives one peak, so four carbons with three peaks means two carbons share an environment. A carbon does not go missing from the spectrum: carbons that look alike simply share a peak.

b.q: Ethanol, CH3CH2OH, and methoxymethane, CH3OCH3, are isomers. How many peaks would each show in a carbon-13 NMR spectrum?
opts: Ethanol has two peaks and methoxymethane has one
Ethanol has one peak and methoxymethane has two
Both have two peaks, as both have two carbons
Both have one peak, as both have the same formula
b.why: In ethanol the two carbons are bonded differently, so there are two environments. In methoxymethane both carbons are bonded to the oxygen and one other carbon-free CH3 group in the same way, so they are equivalent and give one peak. The same number of carbons does not mean the same number of peaks.
b.clue: Draw each molecule and ask if the two carbons look identical.

a.best: Two of the carbons are in the same environment

b.best: Ethanol has two peaks and methoxymethane has one

problems.detail: Why (b) says each methoxymethane carbon is bonded to 'the oxygen and one other carbon-free CH3 group', which is muddled and inaccurate. Each carbon is bonded to the oxygen and three hydrogens, and the oxygen links it to the other CH3 group. It should say both CH3 groups are attached to the same oxygen in the same way, so they are equivalent.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear answer. The explanation for question b describes methoxymethane's bonding in a confusing, inaccurate way and should be reworded.
